title: Vasquez: adoration's one act has exterior mark plus interior affect of submission
source_text: LIII. Caeterum, quod etiam ex jam dictis satis colligitur, observat idem Vasquez, actum adorationis duobus constare. Unum est nota exterior submissionis, ut genuflexio, capitis apertio, &c. Alterum est submissionis affectus, quo quis ex apprehensione excellentiae, & dignitatis, alicui ut excellenti, notam illam vult exhibere; sine quo nota exterior non esset adoratio, & cultus; cum ea fieri posset animo quoque joci aut irrisionis. Nec enim nota exterior, & interior affectus submissionis, duae sunt adorationes: sed ex utroque unus actus reverentiae & honoris constat: sicut in universum actus virtutis, interiori, & exteriori constituitur.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover, which is also sufficiently gathered from what has already been said, the same Vasquez observes that the act of adoration consists of two things. One is the exterior mark of submission, as genuflection, uncovering of the head, and so on. The other is the affect of submission, by which someone from the apprehension of excellence and dignity wills to exhibit that mark to someone as excellent; without which the exterior mark would not be adoration and cult; since it could also be done with a mind of jest or mockery. For the exterior mark and the interior affect of submission are not two adorations: but from both one act of reverence and honor consists: just as in general an act of virtue is constituted by the interior and the exterior.
pass_b_english: Vasquez: one adoration-act has two parts—exterior mark (kneel, bare the head) plus interior affect of submission.
Without the affect, the gesture is not cult (it could be a joke); both together make one honor-act, as virtue's interior and exterior do.
